reuse.why: The change reuses recurrence conversion and date adjustment helpers, but repeats the daily skipping policy across three consumers instead of sharing it.

duplication.why: Daily nonworking-day selection is implemented separately in getNextDate, getUpcomingDates, and getDatesInRange.

placement.why: Holiday matching belongs in shared/schedules.ts, but server handlers also own recurrence policy that should live alongside those shared helpers.

scope.why: All edits concern the requested schedule rules, range handler, configuration propagation, or accompanying tests.

maintainability.why: Maintainers must coordinate several differently structured implementations of the same scheduling policy, while the new handler leaves its existing RecurConfig contract implicit.

bypasses_abstraction.where: getUpcomingDates and getDatesInRange rebuild the nonworking-day predicate instead of using isNonWorkingDay; schedule-template.ts bypasses getNextDate adjustment and retains its own adjustment policy.

disguised_duplication.where: The same daily skipping decision appears as a while condition in getNextDate, a filter in getUpcomingDates, and an if/continue branch in getDatesInRange.

abstraction_drift.where: getDateWithSkippedWeekend gains a holidays parameter; getNextDate gains daily skipping, a holiday-presence conditional, and a non-daily adjustment guard, while getUpcomingDates, getDatesInRange, and schedule-template.ts retain independent policy paths.
